subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards remain full-content-only with a better cadence/backpressure fix, or should OpenClaw add an explicit opt-in append/delta mode for deployments where full payloads are too slow?
rationale: The official CardKit docs and prior truncation fixes support full-content updates, but current live evidence says full-content updates can be unusably slow and the open coalescing PR may be insufficient; choosing an escape hatch is a product and compatibility decision, not a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Approve an opt-in append mode
options.body: Keep full content as the default but allow explicitly configured deployments to use append/delta payloads with live Feishu proof and documentation of the compatibility risk.

options.title: Stay full-content-only
options.body: Continue treating full-content CardKit updates as the only supported transport and require a stronger cadence/backpressure implementation with live latency proof before landing.

options.title: Document streaming-off workaround only
options.body: Avoid new transport behavior for now and direct affected deployments to disable streaming cards until a proven owner-backed design exists.

recommendation.title: Approve an opt-in append mode
recommendation.body: Keep full content as the default but allow explicitly configured deployments to use append/delta payloads with live Feishu proof and documentation of the compatibility risk.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata names this handle as the Feishu plugin maintainer, and the decision is specific to Feishu/Lark channel transport behavior.
